claims.text: This is a single trip before the tribunal: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00537, and the trace's first fix (2026-09-25T21:06:40+08:00) is the trip_record's started_at, so the POL-RD-08(a) same-trip limb is satisfied and the rider's claim is properly constituted.

The rider rests its distance case on a clean trace: EV-GPS-00537 records coverage_pct 100, 115 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, max_gap_sec 0.0 and an empty gaps list, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires, the trace is not impaired for policy purposes, and its admissibility weight is 1.0.

Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance is the trace figure, gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 4.59 km, and not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 4.6 km; the rider puts the distance case on the field the clause names and does not ask the tribunal to decide anything on the convenience copy.

Measured on that governing trace the excess over the booked optimal is 0.09 km, or 2.00% of the 4.5 km optimal, which is below both POL-RD-01 gates (greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms and greater than 20%); the rider does not contend that the driver's route crosses the deviation threshold, and does not press the 0.01 km difference between the trace and the rounded copy.

The rider was billed on 19.0 minutes against an 11.0-minute optimal route - a 73% duration overage - while the distance matched the optimal route to within 0.09 km, and the only admissible traffic artifact, EV-ADVIS-00537-01, is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0), so no admitted evidence explains the extra eight minutes the rider paid for under the 2.2x surge; POL-RD-03 cannot be run against this record because there is no advisory for the driver to invoke.

The rider's contested amount is the charged_total of 28.45 on EV-FARE-00537, set against the platform's own recomputed_fare of 23.361 for the identical trip on the optimal route at the same 2.2x surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown - a 5.089 gap; the rider accepts that POL-RD-02's arithmetic runs only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01, and puts the figure on the record as the measure of what the night surge on a longer-than-optimal drive cost the rider rather than requesting an award the clause does not reach.

No POL-RD-08 corroboration requirement is engaged against the rider on this record: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, far below the four-claim trigger, so this is not a case in which the trace needs independent support before it can be read.

claims.text: The governing distance measurement is the trace, not the meter's rounded copy: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field that decides the threshold test and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for it. The trace records 4.59 km against a booked optimal of 4.5 km, an excess of 0.09 km — 2.00% of optimal. Both establishment gates (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute) fail by an order of magnitude, so no route deviation is established on this trip.

POL-RD-01 is explicit that where either establishment test fails 'no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip'. The trace's own derived deviation status reads 'no deviation'; the rider's grievance is that an identical journey cost more at 9pm, which is a characterisation of price, not a finding of excess distance, and the clause closes the door on it.

POL-RD-02 runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01'. None is, so the 23.3610 recomputed fare, the 5.10 refund and the 0.1789 refund share sitting in the fare ledger's derived block are contingent arithmetic that never ripens into an entitlement; neither the distance term nor the time term (the trip's 19 charged minutes against an 11 minute optimal estimate) can be refunded outside an established deviation.

NO_ACTION is party-relative under POL-GEN-03: it leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are. The ledger shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so on this rider-filed dispute the present state that stands is a standing charge — the outcome the driver contends for.

The whole of the contested amount is explained by surge, not by route: the fare_breakdown records a surge_multiplier of 2.2 on a METERED fare, contributing 12.3060 of surge uplift and producing the 28.45 charge. POL-RD-02 fixes the multiplier's home as fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, the driver's statement is that surge was displayed before booking, and no clause of the route-deviation policy refunds a disclosed multiplier absent an established deviation.

Even at the driver-profile check that POL-RD-06 would require for a material deviation, this driver carries 0 deviation flags over 250 completed trips in the trailing 90 days. The ratio is 0.00, no pattern is established, and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is a near-synonym that POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting for the trailing-window field the clause names.

Nothing in the pass-through layer requires correction: the fare_breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines at all — on-optimal-route and off-optimal-route ERP totals are both 0.00, erp_gantries is empty — and no airport surcharge or fixed surcharge is present. POL-RD-09(4) therefore has no phantom line to refund as a standalone billing-integrity correction, and no referral arises under it.

No mandatory escalation trigger in POL-RD-10 fires. The trip identifier TRP-00537 appears on the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown alike; the trace is complete at 100% coverage with 115 fixes, zero gaps and a 0.0 second maximum gap, so POL-RD-07's integrity limbs are not met; and the event sequence runs strictly forwards (accepted 21:00:40, arrived 21:05:40, started 21:06:40, ended 21:25:40). This case is ruleable on the record and need not be held.

POL-RD-08 puts the initial burden on the rider to show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired gps_trace. The trace here is unimpaired but shows 0.09 km and 2.00% against a 0.8 km and 20% gate, so limb (b) is not discharged and the burden never shifts to the driver to invoke any exculpatory clause.

The rider's yardstick — a 17.70 noon fare for the same journey — appears nowhere in the admitted evidence; the only fare artifact in the pool is this trip's own ledger at 28.45. POL-RD-08 provides that assertions citing no evidence ID carry no weight and are discarded, so the comparison cannot found a finding of overcharging.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: I understand the same journey cost more at 9pm, but on this record the route-deviation claim is not made out. The governing GPS trace (EV-GPS-00537) shows 4.59 km against the booked optimal 4.5 km, an excess of 0.09 km, or 2.0%. POL-RD-01 requires both an excess greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20% before a deviation is established; both gates fail by a wide margin. The trip record's 4.6 km convenience copy is not used for the threshold test. Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02 does not run, and the 23.361 recomputed fare and 5.089 gap in the fare ledger are conditional arithmetic, not a refund. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-00537) shows the charge was 28.45 with a 2.2 surge multiplier; the actual surge amount on the ledger is 15.08. The derived block's 12.306 is the surge component of the optimal-route recomputation, not the actual charged surge line. No clause in the route-deviation policy refunds a disclosed surge multiplier where no deviation is established. Your 17.70 noon comparison and the 39.60/40.60 figures in your narrative are not in the admitted evidence; the only fare artifact is this trip's 28.45 ledger, so I cannot use those comparisons as a ground. The 19-minute actual duration against the 11-minute optimal estimate was charged, but time overage does not by itself establish route deviation or a billing-integrity defect, and no clause refunds it independently. To the driver: the trace is clean (100% coverage, 115 fixes, no gaps), no ERP or surcharge line is present (off-route and on-route ERP totals 0.00 and erp_gantries empty), no chat-log detour request exists, and your profile shows 0 deviation flags over 250 completed trips in 90 days. No exculpatory clause was needed or invoked. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00537-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) is noted; because no closure was asserted, its absence neither creates a refund nor triggers escalation under POL-RD-10(5). The rider-profile corroboration trigger under POL-RD-08 is not engaged (0 deviation claims and 0 substantiated in 60 days). No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral arises, and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. The ruling leaves payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0 as they are. Confidence is 0.95, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the decision (GPS trace, trip record and fare breakdown); the missing advisory carries no weight and is not relied on.

Both of you: this is trip TRP-00537 (Novena Square to Great World, 25 September 2026) and the answer turns on the distance test in POL-RD-01. Rider — I measured it the way the policy requires. The governing distance is the GPS trace, gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 4.59 km on EV-GPS-00537, not the meter's rounded copy (trip_record.actual_distance_km = 4.6 km), because POL-RD-01 says the trace governs and forbids citing the rounded copy for the threshold test. Against the booked optimal of 4.5 km (EV-TRIP-00537) the excess is 0.09 km, or 2.00% of optimal. A deviation is established only when the excess is BOTH more than 20% of optimal AND more than 0.8 km; neither gate is met, and POL-RD-01 provides that where either test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. No refund is available on the distance line, so POL-RD-02 never runs and the 23.361 recomputed fare, the 5.089 gap and the 0.1789 refund share in the ledger are contingent arithmetic that never ripen into an entitlement. Your real grievance is price, not route: the 28.45 charge is fully explained on EV-FARE-00537 by a 3.80 base fare, 10.255 of distance and time charges before surge, the surge multiplier of 2.2 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (a 12.306 surge uplift), and the 0.80 platform fee. No clause of the route-deviation policy refunds a disclosed surge, and your comparison to a 17.70 noon fare is an assertion citing no evidence ID, which POL-RD-08 provides carries no weight. I did note your point that you were charged 19.0 minutes against an 11.0-minute optimal estimate — roughly eight minutes and about 5.09 of the fare — while the distance matched the optimal route almost exactly. That overage sits on the time line, not the distance line, and this policy gives no refund for it; the one traffic artifact that could have explained the road conditions, EV-ADVIS-00537-01, is missing from the record (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0), so the extra eight minutes is an open question rather than a ground for a refund I can award under this policy. Driver — your account that the surge was displayed before booking and that you drove the normal route is consistent with the trace. The POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged because the deviation is not material, and in any event EV-DPROF-00537 shows 0 deviation flags over 250 completed trips in the trailing 90 days, so no pattern arises; I used only the trailing-window fields the clause names, not the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter. Nothing in the pass-through layer needs correction: there are no ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge on EV-FARE-00537, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to refund and no billing-integrity referral arises. No mandatory escalation trigger in POL-RD-10 fires: the trip identifiers all match TRP-00537, the trace is complete (100% coverage, 115 fixes, 0.0 second maximum gap, so POL-RD-07's integrity limbs are not met), and the timestamps run strictly forwards. Outcome: NO_ACTION. The charge stands — fare_breakdown.payment_status remains CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd remains 0.00, so the 28.45 is not refunded and not re-collected.

This ruling is addressed to both parties. Both sides have put the decisive point in issue and the evidence answers it.

DISTANCE (POL-RD-01). The governing measurement is the GPS trace, EV-GPS-00537: trace_distance_km 4.59 km against a booked optimal_distance_km of 4.5 km, an excess of 0.09 km — 2.00% of optimal. POL-RD-01 forbids citing the trip record's rounded copy (actual_distance_km 4.6 km) for the threshold test, and the rider correctly relies on the trace figure instead. Both establishment gates fail by a wide margin: 0.09 km is far below the greater-than-0.8 km absolute gate, and 2.00% is far below the greater-than-20% gate. No route deviation is established, and POL-RD-01 is explicit that where either gate fails the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The driver's account that he drove the normal route is consistent with this.

SURGE AND THE CONTESTED 28.45 (POL-RD-02). The rider's real grievance is that an identical journey cost 17.70 at noon and 28.45 at night. That is a price complaint, not a routing one. The fare_breakdown EV-FARE-00537 shows a METERED fare with surge_multiplier 2.2, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier — the only artifact that carries the field — combining base_fare 3.80, distance_charge 3.375, time_charge 3.08 and the 0.80 platform fee into the 28.45 charged_total, with 12.3060 of surge uplift. POL-RD-02's recomputed_fare of 23.361 and the 5.10 refund sitting in the ledger's derived block run only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01'. None is, so that arithmetic confers no entitlement. The rider's own brief accepts this. No clause of this policy refunds a disclosed surge multiplier, and POL-RD-01 closes the door on re-characterising the trip to reach one. The 17.70 noon comparison appears nowhere in the admitted evidence; under POL-RD-08 an assertion citing no evidence ID carries no weight.

BURDEN (POL-RD-08). The rider satisfies limb (a) — trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry TRP-00537 — but fails limb (b), an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden never shifts to the driver. No corroboration requirement is engaged against the rider either: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, both citable fields under POL-RD-08.

DURATION (POL-RD-03). The rider notes 19.0 charged minutes against an 11.0-minute optimal estimate, a 73% overage. The route-deviation policy measures deviation by distance under POL-RD-01, and extra elapsed time is not a refundable line absent an established deviation. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00537-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT); its absence is citable but it carries no deciding fact here, because POL-RD-03 was not invoked to excuse a deviation and there is no deviation to excuse. The trace is continuous at a 10-second cadence with 100% coverage, 115 fixes, zero gaps and a 0.0 s maximum gap, so no impaired stretch needs bridging and POL-RD-07 is not engaged.

BILLING INTEGRITY (POL-RD-09). There is nothing to correct: on-optimal-route and off-optimal-route ERP totals are both 0.00, erp_gantries is empty, and no airport or fixed surcharge line is present. POL-RD-09(4) has no phantom line to refund and produces no billing-integrity referral.

DRIVER PROFILE (POL-RD-06, POL-GEN-01). No material deviation arises, so the POL-RD-06 check is not even required. In any event the citable trailing-window figures are deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 250 — a ratio of 0.00, no pattern — and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is a context-only near-synonym that POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting for the field the clause names.

ESCALATION (POL-RD-10). No trigger fires. The trip identifiers match across all three artifacts; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c); timestamps run strictly forward (accepted 21:00:40, arrived 21:05:40, started 21:06:40, ended 21:25:40); no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing artifact; the refund is zero, well under 150.00 and under charged_total; the parties do not contradict each other; and every charge line has its counterpart in the trace and trip record. This case is ruleable and need not be held.

OUTCOME. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative: the filing party's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands. On this rider-filed dispute that leaves payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0 as they are. No refund issues to the rider, and no driver compensation arises — the rider was billed 4.6 km against a 4.59 km trace, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall. Confidence is 0.9, capped at 1.0 by the weight of the artifacts that carry the deciding fact (EV-GPS-00537 and EV-TRIP-00537, both weight_multiplier 1.0).

ruling.explanation: To the rider: your complaint is that an identical journey cost 17.70 at noon and 28.45 at 9pm, and you ask how that is not overcharging. The policy that governs a route-deviation dispute tests the route by distance, and on this trip's own evidence the route was correct. The governing figure is the GPS trace, not the meter's rounded copy: EV-GPS-00537 (weight 1.0) records trace_distance_km 4.59, and the booked optimal on EV-TRIP-00537 (weight 1.0) is 4.5 km. That is an excess of 0.09 km, or 2.00% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND greater than 20% of optimal; here both gates fail, so no deviation exists and POL-RD-01 directs the outcome to NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. That disposes of the contingent arithmetic you placed on the record: the fare ledger's own recomputed_fare of 23.3610 and the 5.089 gap to the 28.45 charged_total are figures POL-RD-02 produces only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01, and none is. The same answer covers your duration point — 19 charged minutes against an 11.0-minute optimal estimate: POL-RD-01 measures deviation by distance, and no clause refunds a time overage on a trip where the distance matches the optimal route. Your POL-RD-08 point is correct and recorded: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so no independent-corroboration requirement is engaged against you; it simply does not create an excess where the trace measures none. Your POL-RD-03 point (the extra eight minutes are unexplained because the only traffic artifact, EV-ADVIS-00537-01, is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0) is also recorded, but POL-RD-03 is an exculpatory clause a driver invokes for a closure, and the driver has invoked none; a MISSING artifact carries no fact under POL-GEN-02(3) and its absence opens no refund route. Your 17.70 noon comparison appears nowhere in the admitted evidence — the only fare artifact in the pool is this trip's own ledger at 28.45 — so it cannot found a finding, as POL-RD-08 provides. To the driver: the case is decided in your favour on the same distance finding, and your account that you drove the normal route is consistent with the trace. The contested amount is explained by surge, not by route: EV-FARE-00537 records surge_multiplier 2.2 on a METERED fare producing the 28.45 charge, and no clause of this policy refunds a disclosed multiplier absent an established deviation. The driver_profile check in POL-RD-06 is not reached because no material deviation exists, but on the field the clause names you carry 0 deviation flags across 250 completed trips in the trailing 90 days, so no pattern could have been established; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is not substituted. POL-RD-09 requires no correction: the fare_breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines (on- and off-optimal-route totals both 0.00, erp_gantries empty) and no surcharge, so there is no phantom line to refund and no billing-integrity referral arises. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifier TRP-00537 is common to trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is complete at 100% coverage, 115 fixes at a 10-second cadence, zero gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) do not bite and no corroboration question arises; the timestamps run strictly forward; and no exculpatory clause has been invoked against a missing artifact. The present state therefore stands as POL-GEN-03 requires on a rider-filed dispute: payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0 are left exactly as they are, and no money moves. Confidence is 0.9: the deciding fact — that the driven distance matched the optimal route to within 0.09 km — is carried by two full-weight artifacts, EV-GPS-00537 and EV-TRIP-00537, so the cap is 1.0 and the ruling sits well above the 0.70 floor.

The rider rests its distance case on a clean trace: EV-GPS-00537 records coverage_pct 100, 115 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, max_gap_sec 0.0 and an empty gaps list, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires, the trace is not impaired for policy purposes, and its admissibility weight is 1.0.

Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance is the trace figure, gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 4.59 km, and not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 4.6 km; the rider puts the distance case on the field the clause names and does not ask the tribunal to decide anything on the convenience copy.

Measured on that governing trace the excess over the booked optimal is 0.09 km, or 2.00% of the 4.5 km optimal, which is below both POL-RD-01 gates (greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms and greater than 20%); the rider does not contend that the driver's route crosses the deviation threshold, and does not press the 0.01 km difference between the trace and the rounded copy.

The rider was billed on 19.0 minutes against an 11.0-minute optimal route - a 73% duration overage - while the distance matched the optimal route to within 0.09 km, and the only admissible traffic artifact, EV-ADVIS-00537-01, is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0), so no admitted evidence explains the extra eight minutes the rider paid for under the 2.2x surge; POL-RD-03 cannot be run against this record because there is no advisory for the driver to invoke.

The rider's contested amount is the charged_total of 28.45 on EV-FARE-00537, set against the platform's own recomputed_fare of 23.361 for the identical trip on the optimal route at the same 2.2x surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown - a 5.089 gap; the rider accepts that POL-RD-02's arithmetic runs only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01, and puts the figure on the record as the measure of what the night surge on a longer-than-optimal drive cost the rider rather than requesting an award the clause does not reach.

No POL-RD-08 corroboration requirement is engaged against the rider on this record: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, far below the four-claim trigger, so this is not a case in which the trace needs independent support before it can be read.

The governing distance measurement is the trace, not the meter's rounded copy: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field that decides the threshold test and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for it. The trace records 4.59 km against a booked optimal of 4.5 km, an excess of 0.09 km — 2.00% of optimal. Both establishment gates (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute) fail by an order of magnitude, so no route deviation is established on this trip.

POL-RD-01 is explicit that where either establishment test fails 'no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip'. The trace's own derived deviation status reads 'no deviation'; the rider's grievance is that an identical journey cost more at 9pm, which is a characterisation of price, not a finding of excess distance, and the clause closes the door on it.

POL-RD-02 runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01'. None is, so the 23.3610 recomputed fare, the 5.10 refund and the 0.1789 refund share sitting in the fare ledger's derived block are contingent arithmetic that never ripens into an entitlement; neither the distance term nor the time term (the trip's 19 charged minutes against an 11 minute optimal estimate) can be refunded outside an established deviation.

NO_ACTION is party-relative under POL-GEN-03: it leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are. The ledger shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so on this rider-filed dispute the present state that stands is a standing charge — the outcome the driver contends for.

The whole of the contested amount is explained by surge, not by route: the fare_breakdown records a surge_multiplier of 2.2 on a METERED fare, contributing 12.3060 of surge uplift and producing the 28.45 charge. POL-RD-02 fixes the multiplier's home as fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, the driver's statement is that surge was displayed before booking, and no clause of the route-deviation policy refunds a disclosed multiplier absent an established deviation.

Even at the driver-profile check that POL-RD-06 would require for a material deviation, this driver carries 0 deviation flags over 250 completed trips in the trailing 90 days. The ratio is 0.00, no pattern is established, and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is a near-synonym that POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting for the trailing-window field the clause names.
